This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER Heard with the aid of case diary.
This is first application filed under Section 438 Cr.P.C seeking anticipatory bail, as the applicant/accused is apprehending his arrest in connection with FIR/Crime No.740/2023 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station-Kothwali, District- Dewas (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(N) and 506 of the IPC.
2. Prosecution story in brief is that the prosecutrix had already married in year 2009.
She had no children by 2017.
She came in contact with the applicant in year 2017 by Facebook and he was working in police department as a constable.

At that time she used to live separately due to family Rahul Raghuwanshi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92508056/

sentences.text: The applicant on the pretext of love, induced her to meet.
Because of good friendship, she agreed to meet him.
They used to meet at distinct places and developed physical relation as well.
In year 2018, because of the disputes between prosecutrix and her husband, she got apart from him.
Her husband had filed divorce case in competent court.
In year 2019, when the applicant was transferred to Dewas, the prosecutrix started living with him as a wife in a rented room.
The applicant had promised her to marry when she gets divorced.

Even after living together for 4 years,
the applicant did not marry her.
On 27/01/2023, applicant married to the prosecutrix in ostentatious manner.
On 10/02/2023, the applicant had left the place stating her sister's marriage as reason and thereafter, the applicant as well left for her village.
By this the applicant since 2017 - 2023 on the false pretext of marriage the applicant had sexual intercourse with the prosecutrix but later on did not marry her.
Therefore, the matter was reported by the prosecutrix.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant/ accused submits that, the applicant has not committed the offence and has falsely been implicated in the case.

The prosecutrix was already a married woman,
therefore, without getting divorce, no question of marriage with her arises.
The prosecutrix was consenting party for sexual intercourse.
The applicant is serving in M.P. Police department as a constable, so there stands no chance that he will abscond.
The applicant has no criminal antecedents.
The prosecutrix had also filed written complaint to Mahila P/S, Dewas but after inquiry, the complaint was found to be false.
The applicant had given Rs.1,70,000/- to the prosecutrix through her bank account (Annexure A-4) and a necklace of Rs.2,92,950/- (Annexure A-5).
The prosecutrix had told the applicant, that she is Hindu, but after some time, the applicant came to know that she is from different community.
She started blackmailing the applicant.
Therefore, the applicant had filed a complaint case (Annexure A-6) for the offence punishable u/s 294, 323, 506, 384 of IPC against the prosecutrix.
If the applicant is arrested, his career will be affected.
Therefore, it is prayed that the applicant be granted anticipatory bail.
4. On other hand learned counsel for the objector as well as the learned counsel for the non-applicant/state have objected the prayer.
Learned counsels have submitted that the prosecutrix had transferred Rs.7,000/- and Rs.5,000/- via Google Pay on 23/02/2023 and 20/03/2023 respectively on being demanded by the applicant.
When the prosecutrix came to know that the applicant is giving excuses to marry her, then she stated that she will complain against him to the police.
Then the applicant had intimidated her, that if she complains, he will viral the videos of the prosecutrix and kill her.
On the basis of the application filed by the objector, offence u/s 66 and 67 of the I.T. Act, 2000, has been added.
Mobile phone of the applicant is to be seized.
Learned counsel for the objector has also submitted that from time to time the prosecutrix has transferred a total of Rs.1,64,250/- in bank account given by the applicant on his demand.
Therefore, no question for blackmail arises by the prosecutrix to the applicant.
Therefore, he is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

5. Having heard learned counsels for the parties, perused the case-diary also considering the facts and circumstances of the case, in view of this court, it is a fit case to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Resultantly, without commenting upon the merits, application for anticipatory bail is allowed.
